name: UGC 3165, SNhunt151 field (Hubble)
blurb: UGC 3165, the host galaxy of the transient SNhunt151, seen by Hubble.
label: snhunt151-hubble
story: SNhunt151 first looked like a supernova impostor, the outburst of a massive star, but its spectra later resembled a Type IIn supernova. Astronomers suggest it was an explosion inside a dense cocoon of gas the star had shed earlier, much like the nebulae around luminous blue variables such as Eta Carinae.

claims.text: SNhunt151 was first classified as a supernova impostor, a nonterminal outburst of a massive star
Spectroscopically it is a Type IIn supernova
It may be an outburst or explosion inside a dense circumstellar nebula from past mass loss, like those around some luminous blue variables such as Eta Carinae
Other designations PSN J04472985+2358555, XM07BW, CSS131025:044730+235856
Hubble observed SNHUNT151 in a snapshot survey of recent, nearby supernovae that also images SN impostors
